study: Best-effort selective recovery addendum for ignored-backup comparison
question: After native operation-level selective revert, can the tool preserve the cleanup effect on allowed paths and restore every collateral file, including .gitignore-excluded backups?
contract: Both allowed build artifacts must be absent; every other project-file path and byte must equal the pre-command baseline.
arms: agent-rollback native pre/post checkpoints, native op revert of the post-command checkpoint operation, then replay only the command-post state for the two contract-allowed paths
C-SDVR production project(base, observed, allowed) projection
pairing: For each scale, both arms use an exact copy of the same Git-initialized baseline and the same once-executed command-post byte map; byte-map equality is checked before recovery scoring.
limits: One public cleanup task family with three injected file-count scales; not an independent task cohort.
The agent-rollback arm includes explicit contract-aware replay of allowed post-command paths to give its native selective revert a fair chance to meet the same joint output contract.
Results apply to the pinned commit and its default Git-aware scanner, which honors .gitignore.
